card.name: Joropo
card.tagline: Venezuelan and Colombian plains — harp, cuatro, maracas, and a heel-toe stomp built for hard ground.
card.profile: The joropo, better known as Música Llanera, is a musical style resembling the fandango, and an accompanying dance. It originated in the Llanos of Colombia and Venezuela 300 years ago and it has African, European and Native South American influences. There are different joropo variants: tuyero, oriental, and llanero. It is a fundamental genre of Venezuelan música criolla. It is also the most popular "folk rhythm": the well-known song "Alma Llanera" is a joropo, considered the unofficial national anthem of Venezuela. In 1882 it became Venezuela's national dance and music.
card.insight: In 2025, UNESCO inscribed Venezuelan joropo on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The Colombian Congress declared joropo as “Cultural Heritage of the Nation” in 2025 and designated May 24 as National Joropo Day.
